T4.8.message: The opening sentence is stilted and says the same thing twice: 'One of Kāśī's stories about its Lord: the Kūrma Purāṇa tells a story set in Vārāṇasī, Kāśī's city.' It says 'story' twice in one sentence, and 'Vārāṇasī, Kāśī's city' reads awkwardly, since the two names refer to the same city. The rubric fails stilted sentences.
T4.8.suggested_fix: Use one clear sentence, e.g. 'Kāśī has its own stories about its Lord. The Kūrma Purāṇa tells one set in Vārāṇasī, as Kāśī is also called.' Or simply: 'The Kūrma Purāṇa tells a story of Kāśī's Lord set in Vārāṇasī.' Make the matching change in body.hi ('कूर्म पुराण काशी के स्वामी की एक कथा कहता है, जो वाराणसी में घटती है।').

T4.8.message: Agreement slip: two subjects ('जगत् ... और एतत् ...') take a singular verb ('वह है जिस पर वे कर्म करते हैं'). It reads as slightly ungrammatical Hindi.
T4.8.suggested_fix: 'जगत् "संसार" और एतत् "यह" मिलकर वह बताते हैं जिस पर वे कर्म करते हैं; एकः "अकेले" अगली पंक्ति के त्वम् "आप" के साथ जाता है।'

T4.8.message: '"दधा" की दोहराई' uses an unusual noun form. In modern Hindi the usual word is 'दोहराव' (or 'द का दोहराया जाना'), so 'दोहराई' reads oddly.
T4.8.suggested_fix: '"दधा" में "द" का दोहराव इस धातु के वर्तमान रूप की पहचान है।'
